scope: Bounded review of §10.6 aggregate / §10.6.1–.4 screen applicability, §10.6.5 halftone dictionary transfer-function paths (not screen generation), and §10.8.1–.3 separations and user-requested separation simulation. It reuses the rendering_intent_transfer_current source/assertion review for Table 128–132 TransferFunction details and does not audit §8.6.7 or all of §11 overprint/transparency.

locators.title: Type 1, 6, 10, 16 and 5 halftones; Tables 128–132
locators.location: printed pp.374–379 / physical pp.389–394; Table 132 spans printed pp.380–381 / physical pp.395–396

effective_ec3: EC3 #310 physically annotates Table 129 (Type 6) on p.391 / printed p.376 and Table 132 on p.395 / printed p.380. It adds producer constraints around TransferFunction for nonprimary/nonstandard primary components and the Type 5 subdictionary. These changes do not turn the halftone screen into a required feature or change the reader's §10.5 transfer-function obligation.
EC3 #12 on physical p.395 / printed p.380 clarifies that the Type 5 child halftone shall not itself be Type 5; producer-side table language.

EC3 #311 on physical p.396 / printed p.381 strikes the entire Type 5 contrast paragraph, including its nonprimary-colourant fallback. The earlier rendering_intent_transfer_current shard correctly limits its asserted current screen/transfer behavior and does not rely on the struck fallback.

A direct annotation inventory of primary physical pp.380–401 found no Issue-tagged annotations in §10.6.1–.4 or §10.8. The page annotations in this span include links, EC3 #310/#12/#311, and PDF Association tracking annotations; they are not additional normative corrections.

features.source: §10.1 makes applying PDF-defined halftoning conditional on the raster output device supporting it. §10.6.1 says continuous-tone devices need no halftoning and transmit transfer-corrected components directly; §10.6.2 identifies fully on/off output components as the discrete screen case. §10.6.5.1 separately permits a processor to ignore some or all file halftones and use device-suited screens.
features.ledger: §10.6 aggregate is implemented; §10.6.1–.4 are inapplicable; screen generation is not implemented. The row cites ADR 1535 and the owner-accepted RFC 0009 §2.4 rationale.
features.implementation: The processor's raster outputs are continuous-tone 8-bit RGB; toolkit/print output sends that raster downstream, and Route A sends a PDF to another renderer. The application does not generate bilevel/low-bit-depth device pixels or itself drive a halftoning device.
features.assessment: The inapplicable classification is tied to the standard's output-device premise and explicitly addresses the print path: this program produces an 8-bit RGB raster and delegates any printer screening to the platform/driver; it does not claim that a physical printer is continuous-tone. The identified flip route is the program itself generating discrete device pixels. This is a scoped owner decision supported by the active print architecture, not a universal claim that printers never require halftones.
residuals: Reopen if the program adds direct printer/press control, a one-bit or low-bit-depth output raster, or a route that expects this processor to create PDF-defined screens.
The §10.6.5.1 ignore permission is optional device/screen behavior; it does not waive the separate §10.5 transfer functions or their halftone-dictionary TransferFunction entry.

features.source: §10.5 requires the transfer mapping and says a TransferFunction in a halftone dictionary overrides the corresponding graphics-state function. §10.6.5 Tables 128–132 carry that entry in each halftone type; Type 5 selects component/colourant entries and Default for remaining components. Screen parameters are ignored under the device/permission rationale above.
features.ledger: §10.6.5 and .1–.6 are implemented for the TransferFunction content; §10.5 is implemented. The detailed assertion review is in rendering_intent_transfer_current.
features.implementation: crates/pdf-model/src/content/ext_gstate.rs::halftone_transfer and component_transfer preserve the separate `/TR` and `/HT` states. Type 5 selects RGB names and Default; other recognized dictionary types contribute their component transfer; result reaches the transfer map consumed by raster backends.
features.assertion_quality: Existing direct HT override tests inspect a display-list map through a helper rather than exercising the raster consumer. rendering_intent_transfer_current drafted public raster tests for Type 5 and Type 6 stream transfer overrides, four distinct TR component maps, and TR2 precedence; that earlier shard owns those drafts and no duplicate is made here. Parent execution status was not independently checked.
features.assessment: No sampled required screen behavior is missing for this continuous-tone raster output. The transfer-function carrier path is implemented; public consumer assertion strength is the residual already recorded by the earlier shard.

features.source: §10.8.1 says subtractive device output may be produced as one separation per colourant and expressly leaves whether to produce them to processing software. §10.8.2 describes Separation/DeviceN overprint behavior for separations and says alternate colour spaces are supplied so prepress-prepared files can display on other devices; on displays that ignore overprint, appearance may differ, with cyan then yellow as the example.
features.ledger: §10.8.1 and .2 implemented; §8.6.6 and §8.6.7 own the colour-space and overprint details beyond this bounded shard.
features.implementation: The optional separation simulation creates process/spot planes under a reader preference. Ordinary screen mode uses alternate-space behavior. Screen and simulated press routes have distinct asserted controls.
features.assessment: This shard finds the optional screen default and the alternate/press distinction explicitly exercised. Detailed overprint operation semantics are not re-certified here.

features.source: §10.8.3 says a simulation can be performed when closer matching matters; its results should match four steps: (a) process as a subtractive process-colour/optional spot simulated device and determine its colours, consulting default DestOutputProfile or ColorantTable values where available; (b) convert every separation to flat XYZ on all-white matte; (c) multiply blend them; (d) convert/output to the actual device colour space. This is optional (`can`, `should`), distinct from an implementation capability requirement in Table 275 SeparationSimulation.
features.ledger: §10.8 aggregate and .3 are marked implemented; Table 275's SeparationSimulation is marked met by the current static capability map.
features.implementation: ViewState carries a default-off Separations preference. `simulated_press` uses a four-channel page/catalog output-intent ICC profile when available, otherwise the assumed press. Spot planes are discovered from page resources; process and spot planes feed the CPU separation resolver. The resolver converts to flat XYZ, normalizes by white matte, multiplies separations, and maps back to sRGB. GPU explicitly refuses a separated display list by name.
assertions: crates/pdf-model/tests/spot_planes.rs and spot_press.rs source-derived plane/overprint pixels
features.assertion_quality: Numerical oracles are independently reasoned: two sRGB neutral 0.5 separations each map to linear 0.214041, multiply to 0.045814, and return as about 0.237012/60; a zero-tint white plane must be an identity; press cyan/yellow and spot/process controls assert visible distinctions. These are stronger than shared implementation tables, though they do not certify every profile, object type, or backend.
features.assessment: The selected positive paths for all four steps have visible consumer tests and source-derived expectations. Reader preference is correctly distinct from a document's Table 275 capability requirement. No new valid-input failure was established in this bounded audit.
residuals: Step a says default DestOutputProfile or ColorantTable values, when available for a subtractive device, should be consulted. The process route reads a four-channel output-intent profile or assumed press; no ICC ColorantTable/named-colour consumer was found. This is a SHOULD-level recommendation path and is reported as an implementation/ledger qualifier, not a mandatory SHALL defect.
No direct test was built for a ColorantTable-only profile; applicable ICC profile provenance and named-colour interpretation need separate review before promotion as a behavior failure.
This audit does not certify all ICC process profiles, all shading/image/function combinations, 16 spot-plane resource boundaries, or the GPU's deliberate separation-list refusal.
